senses.definition: a small processor built into a car, camera, appliance or instrument, running it without any visible screen
senses.definitionCN: 装在汽车、相机、家电或仪器内部的小型处理器，不通过可见屏幕也能运转该设备
senses.example: The braking system hides a computer that adjusts pressure many times a second.
senses.exampleCN: 刹车系统里藏着一台计算机，每秒多次调整压力。
senses.why: Once a chip could compute, anything that ran itself was said to have a computer inside, even with no keyboard at all.
senses.whyCN: 芯片能算之后，任何自行运转的东西都被说成里面有一台计算机，哪怕根本没有键盘。

senses.title: A machine that imitates a real system
senses.definition: a machine used to imitate a real system, such as weather, traffic or a crash, so that its behaviour can be studied
senses.definitionCN: 用来模仿天气、交通或碰撞等真实系统的机器，以便研究其行为
senses.example: A weather computer ran the storm forward six hours to test the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 一台气象计算机把风暴向前推演六小时，用来检验警报。
senses.why: A simulation is calculation over a model, so the machine that carries it out is named by what it does rather than by its size.
senses.whyCN: 模拟就是对模型做计算，执行它的机器便按功能得名，而不按体积得名。

senses.title: The technology as a force in society
senses.titleCN: 作为社会力量的这门技术
senses.definition: the technology as a whole, treated as something that reshapes work, schooling and daily habits
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机技术整体看作重塑工作、教育与日常习惯的力量
senses.example: The computer changed how offices store and share documents.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机改变了办公室存储与共享文件的方式。
senses.why: Speakers often drop the plural and speak of the machine as a historical agent, which turns a countable device into a mass noun.
senses.whyCN: 说话人常不用复数，而把这台机器当成历史行动者，可数设备于是变成不可数的整体。

senses.title: The mind treated as a machine
senses.definition: the metaphor in which the mind or brain is described as a machine that processes information
senses.definitionCN: 把心灵或大脑描述成处理信息的机器的隐喻
senses.example: The old debate asked whether a brain is really a computer.
senses.exampleCN: 那场旧争论追问大脑是否真是一台计算机。
senses.why: If thought is calculation, then the thing that thinks can be called by the name of the thing that calculates.
senses.whyCN: 如果思维就是计算，那么思考者也可以借用计算者的名字。

intro.en: Computer joins the verb compute, from Latin computare 'to reckon together', with the agent suffix -er. For two centuries the word meant a person who calculates. The machine sense appears in the late nineteenth century and the electronic sense in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computer 由动词 compute 加施事后缀 -er 构成，compute 出自拉丁 computare「一起核算」。此后两个世纪，这个词都指做计算的人。机器义出现在十九世纪末，电子计算机义出现在二十世纪四十年代。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare meant 'to reckon, count, think', and it also yields repute, dispute and impute; reckoning and thinking share one root.
items.cn: putare 意为「核算、计数、思考」，也衍生出 repute、dispute 与 impute；核算与思考共用同一个词根。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare produced computare, 'to reckon together, sum up', the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来核算、求和」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: Computus was the noun for a reckoning, and it survived in medieval Latin for the calculation of church dates.
items.cn: computus 是表示「核算」的名词，在中世纪拉丁语里用于推算教会节期。

items.en: Old French compter 'to count, reckon' carried the word into English, where compute appeared in the seventeenth century as a bookish verb.
items.cn: 古法语 compter「计数、核算」把这个词带进英语，compute 在十七世纪作为书面动词出现。

items.en: The -er form named a person, not a device: a computer was someone employed to work through long calculations.
items.cn: -er 形式当时指人而不指装置：a computer 就是受雇做完长串计算的人。

items.en: Mechanical calculators were already called computers in the late nineteenth century, and electronic machines took the name in the 1940s; first citation uncertain: the exact earliest citation for a machine is not settled.
items.cn: 十九世纪末机械计算器已被叫作计算机，二十世纪四十年代电子机器沿用此名；首见年代不确定：机器义最早书证的具体年份尚无定论。

note.en: Group one is the compute family, where each member names a different grammatical role of the same act; group two holds the everyday rivals for a machine that calculates.
note.cn: 第一组是 compute 词族，每个成员指同一动作的不同语法角色；第二组是日常语言里与「会计算的机器」竞争的词。

entries.definition: To work out an answer by calculation; the verb underneath the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 通过计算得出结果；是名词底下的那个动词。

entries.definition: The act or field of using calculating machines, with no countable device attached.
entries.definitionCN: 使用计算设备的行为或领域，不指某一台可数的装置。

entries.definition: Describing a method or approach that belongs to calculation, rather than naming the machine.
entries.definitionCN: 形容属于计算的方法或路径，而不是给机器命名。

entries.definition: Said of a problem or number that a procedure can in principle work out.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个问题或数值原则上可由某个程序算出。

entries.definition: A small device for arithmetic; it does not store files or run general programs.
entries.definitionCN: 做算术的小装置；不存文件，也不运行通用程序。

entries.definition: A machine defined by answering requests from other machines, whatever its size.
entries.definitionCN: 以回应其他机器请求来定义的机器，与体积无关。

entries.definition: A large central machine of the older style, close to the server sense but tied to a room-sized design.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式的大型中心机器，接近服务器义，但绑定机房规模的设计。

entries.definition: A powerful single-user machine for technical work, between a personal computer and a server.
entries.definitionCN: 供技术工作使用的强力单用户机器，介于个人电脑与服务器之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the agent suffix, the person who calculates, and the machine that took over the same job.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：施事后缀、做计算的那个人，以及接手同一份活的机器。

normal.en: Compute plus -er: the one who computes.
normal.cn: compute 加 -er：做计算的那一位。

normal.en: Before machines, a computer was a job title for a person.
normal.cn: 在没有机器之前，computer 是一个人的职位名称。

normal.en: The same suffix gives teacher, writer and worker.
normal.cn: 同一个后缀还造出 teacher、writer 与 worker。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: personal computer, computer program, computer network.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：个人电脑、计算机程序、计算机网络。

normal.en: A hidden processor in a car is still called its computer.
normal.cn: 汽车里藏着的处理器仍被叫作它的计算机。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk with columns of figures, then picture a cabinet doing the same columns in a second.
abstract.cn: 先想象一个面对成列数字的职员，再想象一个机柜用一秒钟做完同样的列。

abstract.en: Picture a room-sized machine shrinking until it fits under a wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一台占满房间的机器不断缩小，最后能戴在手腕上。

abstract.en: Picture a brain drawn as a circuit board, wires where nerves used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象把大脑画成一块电路板，神经的位置换成了导线。

examples.en: The first computers in the observatory were people, not machines.
examples.cn: 天文台最早的 computer 是人，不是机器。

examples.en: A single computer can now hold the archive that once filled a building.
examples.cn: 如今一台计算机就能装下曾经占满一栋楼的档案。

examples.en: Engineers debate whether the brain is a computer or only behaves like one.
examples.cn: 工程师们争论大脑究竟是一台计算机，还是只是表现得像一台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（一起）+ put（放）+ er（者）」——把数字放在一起算的那台机器：计算机

root: 拉丁 computare「一起核算」= com-「一起」+ putare「核算、思考」，加施事后缀 -er。同根词有 compute、computation、computable、repute、dispute。十七世纪指人，机器义在十九世纪末出现，电子计算机义在二十世纪四十年代定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one agent that reckons: the electronic machine, the machine on a desk, the person paid to calculate, the central machine, the hidden chip, the simulating machine, the technology as a social force and the mind imagined as a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个「做核算者」：电子机器、桌上的那台、受雇做计算的人、中心机器、藏起来的芯片、做模拟的机器、作为社会力量的技术，以及被想象成机器的心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that performs calculation, first a person, later a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个执行计算的主体，先是人，后来是机器。

branches.en: THE DEVICE ITSELF: the general electronic machine and the personal one are the same sense at different scales of ownership.
branches.cn: 装置本身：通用电子机器与个人电脑，是同一义项在归属尺度上的两种样子。

branches.en: THE HUMAN ANCESTOR: before electronics, the -er pointed at a hired calculator, and that sense survives in histories of science.
branches.cn: 人类祖先：电子设备之前，-er 指向受雇的计算者，这个义项仍活在科学史里。

branches.en: BIG AND TINY: the room-sized central machine and the chip hidden in an appliance are opposite ends of the same function.
branches.cn: 大与小：占满房间的中心机器与家电里藏着的芯片，是同一功能的两个极端。

branches.en: THE MACHINE THAT IMITATES: simulation is calculation run over a model, so the tool is named by its task.
branches.cn: 会模仿的机器：模拟是对模型做计算，工具按任务得名。

branches.en: FROM OBJECT TO IDEA: the technology becomes a social force, and then a metaphor for the mind itself.
branches.cn: 从物件到观念：技术先成为社会力量，再成为心灵的隐喻。

intro.en: Computer is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and an English agent suffix; each piece also builds other common words.
intro.cn: computer 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个英语施事后缀构成，每一部分也都参与构成别的常用词。

latinIntro.en: Com- 'together' joins putare 'to reckon'; the derived computare supplies compute, computation and computer, while -er marks the doer.
latinIntro.cn: com-「一起」与 putare「核算」组合；派生出的 computare 提供 compute、computation 与 computer，-er 则标记执行者。

items.example: The prefix gathers separate numbers into one sum.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的数聚成一个总和。

items.example: Reckoning and thinking grow from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 核算与思考都从这个动词长出来。

items.meaning: to reckon together; to sum up
items.example: Every English member of the family descends from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 这一族的英语成员都出自这个动词。

items.example: Medieval tables of church dates were a computus.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪推算教会节期的表就是一种核算。

items.example: The suffix first marked a person and later a machine.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀先标记人，后来才标记机器。

items.example: The program can compute the total in a moment.
items.exampleCN: 程序一瞬就能算出总数。

items.meaning: the act or result of calculating
items.example: The computation took longer than the writing.
items.exampleCN: 计算花的时间比写作还长。

items.example: Some problems are not computable in finite time.
items.exampleCN: 有些问题无法在有限时间内算出。

items.example: The archive was computerized last year.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆去年完成了计算机化。

items.meaning: the activity of calculating or using machines
items.meaningCN: 计算或使用机器的活动
items.example: Computing moved from rooms to pockets.
items.exampleCN: 计算从机房走进了口袋。

definition_zh: v. 使计算机化，用电脑处理
definition_en: to use computers to do work that people used to do
core_image: 旧档案柜旁搬进一排新电脑
scene: 图书馆把借阅记录全部电脑化。The library computerized all its lending records.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：computerize 指使计算机化；句意是图书馆把借阅记录全部电脑化。

pos.zh: 使计算机化；用电脑处理

senses.title: To do work by computer
senses.definition: to replace manual work with computer systems
senses.definitionCN: 用手工做的事改由电脑完成
senses.example: They computerized the whole inventory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把整个库存电脑化了。
senses.why: Latin computare means to reckon.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 computare 意为计算。

senses.title: To equip with computers
senses.definition: to supply an office or system with computers
senses.definitionCN: 为办公室或系统配备电脑
senses.example: The clinic was computerized last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所去年配上了电脑系统。
senses.why: The sense extends from tasks to places.
senses.whyCN: 该义从任务扩展到场所。

intro.en: Computerize adds a making suffix to computer.
intro.cn: computerize 在 computer 后加上表示「使…」的后缀。

items.en: Putare means to reckon or think.
items.cn: putare 意为计算、思考。

items.en: Computare means to reckon together.
items.cn: computare 意为合计。

items.en: Compute entered English as a verb.
items.cn: 十七世纪 compute 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: Computer named the machine in the 1940s.
items.cn: 二十世纪四十年代 computer 指这种机器。

items.en: Computerize named the changeover.
items.cn: 二十世纪 computerize 指这一转变。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the comput- shape; the near-meaning group names modernising work.
note.cn: 形近组共享 comput- 词形；近义组列出工作现代化。

normalIntro.en: To computerize is to hand work over to computers.
normalIntro.cn: computerize 就是把工作交给电脑。

normal.en: Computare means to reckon.
normal.cn: computare 意为计算。

normal.en: A computer reckons fast.
normal.cn: computer 算得很快。

normal.en: Computerize means give work to computers.
normal.cn: computerize 意为把工作交给电脑。

normal.en: Records can be computerized.
normal.cn: 记录可以电脑化。

normal.en: An office can be computerized.
normal.cn: 办公室也可以电脑化。

abstract.en: A cabinet replaced by a screen.
abstract.cn: 被屏幕取代的档案柜。

abstract.en: Paper files turning into light.
abstract.cn: 纸质档案化作光。

abstract.en: A desk with one new box.
abstract.cn: 桌上多了一台新机器。

examples.en: The firm computerized its payroll.
examples.cn: 公司把工资系统电脑化了。

examples.en: All records are now computerized.
examples.cn: 所有记录现在都已电脑化。

examples.en: They plan to computerize the archive.
examples.cn: 他们计划把档案电脑化。

dict_mnemonic.text: computer（电脑）+ -ize（使…化）→ 使由电脑处理，即计算机化。

root: 拉丁 computare（计算）→ compute → computer → 英语 computerize

sensesIntro.en: Giving tasks to computers, and giving offices computers.
sensesIntro.cn: 把任务交给电脑，以及给办公室配电脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of new computers beside an old filing cabinet
core.cn: 核心意象：旧档案柜旁的一排新电脑

branches.en: Lending records moved to a database.
branches.cn: 转入数据库的借阅记录。

branches.en: Accounts handled by software.
branches.cn: 由软件处理的账目。

branches.en: A clinic fitted with terminals.
branches.cn: 装上终端的诊所。

branches.en: An office wired for computers.
branches.cn: 布好线的办公室。

branches.en: Work and workplace both changed.
branches.cn: 工作与工作场所同时改变。

intro.en: Computerize is built from reckoning pieces; the list adds machine words.
intro.cn: computerize 由「计算」词素构成；下面列出机器词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin putare is to reckon, computare is to reckon together, and digitus is a finger.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 putare 意为计算，computare 意为合计，digitus 意为手指。

latinEntries.exampleCN: computare 产生 compute 与 computer。
putare 促成 compute 与 reputation。
digitus 产生 digit 与 digital。

definition_zh: adj. 凹的，凹面的
definition_en: curving inward like the inside of a bowl
core_image: 一只碗的内侧，光在碗底聚成一点
scene: 这面镜子是凹面的，能把光聚到一点。The mirror is concave and focuses light to a point.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：concave 指凹面的；句意是这面镜子是凹面的，能把光聚到一点。

senses.title: Curving inward
senses.definition: curving in toward the centre, as a bowl does
senses.definitionCN: 像碗一样向内弯向中心
senses.example: A concave lens spreads the light.
senses.exampleCN: 凹透镜使光发散。
senses.why: Latin concavus means hollow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 concavus 意为中空。

senses.title: Hollowed out in shape
senses.definition: having a surface that dips inward
senses.definitionCN: 表面向内凹陷的形状
senses.example: The road is concave after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后路面凹陷下去。
senses.why: The everyday sense describes terrain as well.
senses.whyCN: 日常义也可形容地形。

intro.en: Concave comes from a Latin word meaning hollow.
intro.cn: concave 源自拉丁语「中空」一词。

items.en: Cavus means hollow.
items.cn: cavus 意为中空。

items.en: Concavus means hollowed in.
items.cn: concavus 意为向内中空。

items.en: English used it of curved surfaces.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用它指曲面。

items.en: Optics fixed the mirror and lens senses.
items.cn: 十七世纪光学固定了镜与透镜义。

items.en: Geometry gave it a precise shape.
items.cn: 十九世纪几何学赋予精确形状。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the conc- shape; the near-meaning group names hollow forms.
note.cn: 形近组共享 conc- 词形；近义组列出中空形状。

normalIntro.en: Concave surfaces cave in toward the centre.
normalIntro.cn: concave 的表面向中心「陷」进去。

normal.en: Cavus means hollow.
normal.cn: cavus 意为中空。

normal.en: Concavus means hollowed in.
normal.cn: concavus 意为向内中空。

normal.en: Concave curves inward.
normal.cn: concave 向内弯。

normal.en: A concave mirror gathers light.
normal.cn: 凹面镜聚光。

normal.en: Convex is its opposite.
normal.cn: convex 是它的反义。

abstract.en: The inside of a spoon.
abstract.cn: 勺子内侧。

abstract.en: A bowl holding a little light.
abstract.cn: 盛着一小片光的碗。

abstract.en: A saucer-shaped hollow.
abstract.cn: 碟形的凹坑。

examples.en: The telescope uses a concave mirror.
examples.cn: 这架望远镜用凹面镜。

examples.en: The lens is concave on one side.
examples.cn: 这个透镜一侧是凹的。

examples.en: Rain had made the path concave.
examples.cn: 雨水使小路凹陷。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（向内）+ cavus（中空）→ 向内凹进去的，即凹的。

root: 拉丁 con（向内）+ cavus（中空）→ concavus → 英语 concave

sensesIntro.en: Curving inward like a bowl, in glass or in ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 像碗一样向内弯，无论在玻璃还是地面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the inside curve of a bowl gathering light
core.cn: 核心意象：碗的内侧把光聚拢

branches.en: A mirror that gathers light.
branches.cn: 聚光的镜子。

branches.en: A lens that spreads rays.
branches.cn: 使光线发散的透镜。

branches.en: A path dipped by rain.
branches.cn: 被雨压凹的小路。

branches.en: A saucer of bare earth.
branches.cn: 碟形的裸土。

branches.en: An inward curve, made or found.
branches.cn: 内向的弧，或人造或天成。

intro.en: Concave is built from hollow pieces; the list adds shape words.
intro.cn: concave 由「中空」词素构成；下面列出形状词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus is hollow, concavus is hollowed in, and convexus is arched out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cavus 意为中空，concavus 意为向内凹，convexus 意为向外拱。

latinEntries.exampleCN: concavus 产生 concave。
cavus 产生 cavity 与 excavate。
convexus 产生 convex。

definition_zh: 隐藏；隐瞒；掩盖
definition_en: to hide something or keep it secret
core_image: 一只手把一枚硬币悄悄塞到桌布下面
scene: 她把礼物藏在衣柜最上层，等生日那天再拿出来。He tried to conceal the gift behind the coats.
sceneCN: 这里 conceal 指「藏起」（第 1 个义项：放到看不见的地方）；句意是他想把礼物藏在大衣后面。

senses.title: Hide from sight
senses.definition: to put something where it cannot be seen
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到看不见的地方
senses.example: The camera was concealed in a clock.
senses.exampleCN: 摄像头被藏在一只钟里。
senses.why: The word begins with physical hiding, a thing placed out of view.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指物理上的隐藏，把东西放到视线之外。

senses.title: Keep a fact secret
senses.definition: to keep information from other people
senses.definitionCN: 不让他人知道某些信息
senses.example: She concealed her disappointment.
senses.exampleCN: 她隐瞒了自己的失望。
senses.why: A feeling or fact can be hidden just as a box can be hidden.
senses.whyCN: 情绪或事实能像盒子一样被藏起来。

intro.en: Conceal comes from Latin concelare, to hide completely, built from com-, fully, and celare, to hide.
intro.cn: conceal 来自拉丁语 concelare（完全藏起），由 com-（完全）与 celare（隐藏）构成。

items.en: Celare meant to hide or to keep secret.
items.cn: celare 意为隐藏或保守秘密。

items.en: Concelare strengthened the verb into hiding completely.
items.cn: concelare 把动词强化为完全藏起来。

items.en: Old French concealer carried the strong sense of covering up.
items.cn: 古法语 concealer 保留了严密遮掩的强烈意味。

items.en: English conceal first meant to cover or to keep from sight.
items.cn: 英语 conceal 最初指遮盖或不让看见。

items.en: It now covers hiding facts, feelings and objects alike.
items.cn: 如今它同样覆盖隐藏事实、情绪与物件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to conceal, and the meaning group names other words for keeping something out of view.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 conceal 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他把东西藏起来的词。

entries.definition: to admit that something is true
to decide that something will not happen
to put something where it cannot be seen
to put something over another thing
to hide a feeling or smell

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a coin slipping under a tablecloth, then move to secrets and to hidden feelings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一枚硬币滑到桌布下开始，再走到秘密与被藏起的情绪。

normal.en: Con- makes the hiding complete, and celare is to hide, so conceal is to hide fully.
normal.cn: con- 让隐藏变得彻底，celare 是隐藏，所以 conceal 就是完全藏起来。

normal.en: A concealed camera is there but not seen.
normal.cn: 隐藏的摄像头在那里，却看不见。

normal.en: You can conceal a fact with silence as easily as with a lie.
normal.cn: 用沉默隐瞒事实，和用谎话一样容易。

normal.en: Conceal is more formal than hide, and often suggests intent.
normal.cn: conceal 比 hide 更正式，常暗示有意为之。

normal.en: The noun is concealment, the state of being kept from view.
normal.cn: 名词是 concealment，即被藏在视线之外的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a coin under a cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把硬币推到布下面。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that covers a whole bad day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑容盖住了整个糟糕的日子。

abstract.en: Picture a door painted the same colour as the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门刷成和墙一样的颜色。

examples.en: He concealed the key under a loose stone.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙藏在一块松动的石头下。

examples.en: She could not conceal her surprise.
examples.cn: 她掩饰不住惊讶。

examples.en: The report concealed several important facts.
examples.cn: 这份报告隐瞒了几个重要事实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conceal 记成 con（完全）加 ceal（藏）：把东西完全藏起来，就是隐藏、隐瞒。

root: 源自拉丁语 concelare（com 完全 + celare 隐藏），本义是完全藏起，后指隐藏物件与隐瞒事实、情绪。

sensesIntro.en: From an object put out of sight, to a fact kept from other people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被放到看不见处的物件，到不让他人知道的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sliding a coin under the tablecloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把硬币悄悄推到桌布下面。

branches.en: Physical hiding is the first and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 物理隐藏是第一个也最字面的义项。

branches.en: Information can be treated as an object placed out of view.
branches.cn: 信息可以被当作放到视线之外的物件。

branches.en: A concealed weapon is a legal and physical matter.
branches.cn: 隐藏的武器既涉及法律也涉及物理。

branches.en: A concealed feeling stays inside the person.
branches.cn: 被隐瞒的情绪留在人心里。

branches.en: Both senses depend on someone not seeing or not knowing.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖别人看不到或不知道。

intro.en: Conceal is built on Latin com-, fully, plus celare, to hide, through the French form concealer.
intro.cn: conceal 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 celare（隐藏）构成，经法语 concealer 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hide base cel- also survives in clandestine and cellar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的隐藏词基 cel- 还留在 clandestine 与 cellar 中。

items.example: The wall conceals a small door.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙后藏着一扇小门。

items.example: There was a concealed drawer in the desk.
He was accused of concealing evidence.
The money was kept in concealment.
She used concealer under her eyes.
He spoke concealingly about the trip.
items.exampleCN: 他谈到那次旅行时遮遮掩掩。

items.example: The device is small and concealable.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置很小，便于隐藏。

definition_zh: 承认；让步；让出；失球
definition_en: to admit that something is true, or to allow someone to have something
core_image: 棋手把王轻轻推倒，抬手示意这一局认输
scene: 争论到最后，他点头承认对方说得有道理。He finally conceded that she had a point.
sceneCN: 这里 concede 指「承认」（第 1 个义项：不情愿地承认某事属实）；句意是他最后承认她说的有道理。

senses.title: Admit something is true
senses.definition: to admit that something is true, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 常常不情愿地承认某事属实
senses.example: She conceded that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: To concede is to stop resisting a fact you can no longer deny.
senses.whyCN: 承认就是停止抵抗一个再也无法否认的事实。

senses.title: Hand over a right
senses.definition: to allow someone to have something you held
senses.definitionCN: 允许别人得到你原本拥有的东西
senses.example: The company conceded two seats on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 公司让出了董事会的两个席位。
senses.why: The older sense is yielding ground, and ground can be a seat or a right.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的意思是让出地盘，而地盘也可以是席位或权利。

senses.title: Allow the other side to score
senses.definition: to allow the opposing team to score a goal or point
senses.definitionCN: 让对方球队攻入一球或得到一分
senses.example: The team conceded a goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在最后一分钟失了一球。
senses.why: In sport you yield a point the way an army yields ground.
senses.whyCN: 在运动里让掉一分，就像军队让出阵地。

intro.en: Concede comes from Latin concedere, to go away or give way, built from com-, together, and cedere, to go.
intro.cn: concede 来自拉丁语 concedere（走开、让路），由 com-（一起）与 cedere（走）构成。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to yield or to withdraw.
items.cn: cedere 意为走、让出或退去。

items.en: Concedere meant to give way or to grant a request.
items.cn: concedere 意为让路或应允请求。

items.en: French concéder kept the sense of granting and yielding.
items.cn: 法语 concéder 保留了应允与让出的意思。

items.en: English concede first meant to grant or to admit.
items.cn: 英语 concede 最初指准许或承认。

items.en: Sport added the sense of letting the other side score.
items.cn: 体育又加上了让对方得分的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to concede, and the meaning group names other words for admitting or yielding.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 concede 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示承认与让出的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a chess king tipped over, then move to yielding ground and to a lost goal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推倒的棋子王开始，再走到让出阵地与失球。

normal.en: Con- is together and cede is to go, so to concede is to go away from your own claim.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，cede 是走，concede 就是从自己的主张上退开。

normal.en: To concede a point is to let the other side keep it.
normal.cn: 承认对方一点，就是让对方保住那一点。

normal.en: Concede and cede share the idea of giving ground.
normal.cn: concede 与 cede 都带有让出地盘的意思。

normal.en: A team that concedes a goal has allowed it, not scored it.
normal.cn: 球队 concede 一球，是让对方进球，不是自己进。

normal.en: Concession is the noun, the thing given away.
normal.cn: concession 是名词，即被让出去的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player laying the king on its side.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把王侧放在棋盘上。

abstract.en: Picture one side of a tug of war letting go of the rope.
abstract.cn: 想象拔河的一方松开绳子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening to release a held coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手摊开，放走握着的一枚硬币。

examples.en: He conceded that he had made a mistake.
examples.cn: 他承认自己犯了错。

examples.en: The government conceded several demands.
examples.cn: 政府让步，答应了若干要求。

examples.en: The team conceded twice in the second half.
examples.cn: 球队在下半场失了两球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 concede 记成 con（一起）加 cede（走）：从自己的立场上退开一步，就是让步、承认。

root: 源自拉丁语 concedere（com 一起 + cedere 走），本义是走开、让路，后引申为让出权利、承认事实与在比赛中失球。

sensesIntro.en: From stepping aside, to admitting a fact, and finally to letting the other side score.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让到一边，到承认一个事实，最后到让对方得分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess player tipping the king over to end the game.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋手把王推倒，结束这一局。

branches.en: Admitting a fact is the most common modern sense.
branches.cn: 承认事实是最常见的现代义项。

branches.en: Giving up a right is the older, more physical sense.
branches.cn: 让出权利是更古老、更具体的义项。

branches.en: Sport borrows the same picture of yielding ground.
branches.cn: 体育借用了同一幅让出地盘的画面。

branches.en: Admitting and granting both lower your own claim.
branches.cn: 承认与给予都降低了自己的主张。

branches.en: A seat and a goal are both things you let go.
branches.cn: 席位和进球都是你放手让出的东西。

intro.en: Concede is built on Latin com-, together, plus cedere, to go or yield.
intro.cn: concede 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 cedere（走、让）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin go base ced- also gives proceed, recede and access.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的行走词基 ced- 还给出 proceed、recede 与 access。

items.exampleCN: 那个席位未经争夺就让出了。

items.exampleCN: 这个从句以一个让步词开头。

items.exampleCN: 他是辩论中第一个让步的人。
